hook.line: Turnitin got a new update that lets lecturers set what responsible AI use looks like.
hook.visual: Man in a blue robe talking to camera at home; two-line title 'How to Turnitin/GPTzero proof your essay BEFORE you submit!' on top, Turnitin and GPTZero logo cards bottom.

beats.what: Face with a big how-to title on top and Turnitin and GPTZero logo screenshots in the lower third
Logos drop away; he explains the risk: strict settings can still flag you
Promises a way to make work detector-proof: 'here's how you do that'
Cut to a phone-filmed laptop: finger points at the humanizer site's dashboard URL
Zoom punch on the humanized output with a 'passes major AI detectors' badge row
Cut to the detector's homepage to test the text
Pastes the text into the detector and clicks Scan
Zoom on the result: 'highly confident this text is entirely human'

why_it_works: Opens on a news hook (a new Turnitin update) that creates fear in a specific audience: students about to submit
Brand logos in frame one tell the target viewer instantly that this is about their tools
Ends on the proof: the detector's own 'entirely human' verdict on screen, so the claim is shown, not told
weaknesses: Ethically shaky: teaches bypassing academic integrity checks, a brand risk to copy
No captions for the voice; screen is filmed with a phone and hard to read
Ends abruptly on the result with no follow or save ask
Product plug is undisclosed, which reads as a hidden ad
for_robert: End the demo on the third-party verdict screen as proof, with a zoom punch on the key line; avoid promising to beat a detector or policy.
